summary: Rerun cycle 234 (gelu_noneg + mu_l + LoRA r=8 on all 12 mlp.c_proj) with disjoint calib/eval split to close the cycle 234 data-leakage loop.
strengths: The fix is exactly the fix: calib_ids=all_ids[:200], eval_ids=all_ids[200:300], disjointness asserted by object id and tensor equality.
mu precomputed on calib only; Adam trained on calib only; every PPL print + best-state selection + final_ppl on eval_ids only.
LoRA scaffolding reused verbatim from cycle 234 (r=8, all 12 blocks, 368640 trainable params); only the split changes.
Honest baselines: float ref on eval pre-patch, mu-only init_ppl_eval on eval post-patch; declines to assert init_ppl_eval == 61.664 since that was calib.
Sanity check final_ppl <= init_ppl_eval flagged as signal not assert; if calib training degrades held-out, that is itself the result.
Fallbacks cover wall-time (single seed flag) and data-yield (SEQ_LEN 128->64) without collapsing the experiment.
Verdict thresholds (<=48 CONFIRMED, >=58 REFUTED) published up front, bound-based not narrative-based.
Cycle 234 artefacts preserved per audit requirement.
concerns_nonblocking: Held-out mu-only PPL could land anywhere in ~55-70 depending on which 100 sequences fall in [200:300]; plan correctly refuses to assert a specific value, just ensure JSON records where it actually lands.
3 seeds is the right ambition but single_seed=true fallback must be flagged, not silently dropped.
base_c_proj_0_unchanged check is cheap and catches a real LoraConv1D failure mode; keep it.
decision: APPROVE as written. No changes required. Execute per plan.
